A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViLP benchmark and Image-DPO research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching material across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original human and VLM evaluations, Image-DPO training results, robustness experiments and appendix data analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds a realistic-image experiment and further qualitative failure analysis.

M1.justification: The Image-DPO objective, fixed question-answer pairs, image corruptions and data-generation pipeline remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C. Reference-policy notation is standardized; GPT-4o image generation is used for an added benchmark experiment.

E1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds evaluation on more photorealistic versions of a ViLP subset generated with GPT-4o, extending image-style coverage. The original 900-QIA benchmark and other training and evaluation datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain their comparator membership, including HADPO, RLHF-V, EOS, SIMA, V-DPO and Text-DPO. The realistic-image experiment uses previously evaluated VLMs and introduces no new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: v4 introduces an original-versus-realistic image comparison on a reported subset of 45 QIA pairs using four commercial VLMs. Appendix A.6 additionally requests reasoning before final answers for failure analysis. Existing benchmark metrics and Image-DPO training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds an image-realism ablation, while Appendix A.6 adds six failure cases with model explanations. These extend the retained image-transformation, distractor-fact and corrupted-image Text-DPO analyses.

E5.justification: The Whoops! comparison retains five attempts at temperature 1.0 and the same standard-deviation reporting. The new realistic-image results introduce no repeated-run information, confidence intervals or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Main results in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged. New Table 5 reports subset-specific realistic-minus-original accuracy differences, including ViLPF Score changes of -2.2% for GPT-4o and -4.4% for Claude-3.5-Sonnet. Figure 14 adds six qualitative failure outputs.

T1.justification: The benchmark criteria, Proposition 1 and Appendix B derivations are retained. Adding set braces and standardizing reference-policy notation in Equations 4 and 13 do not change mathematical definitions, assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: ViLP exposes reliance on visual-language priors, humans outperform current VLMs, and Image-DPO improves visual reliance and performance. The additional analyses support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the realism experiment as suggesting that more realistic images can increase task difficulty. Appendix A.6 adds specific explanations involving prior-driven shape recognition, counting, location judgments, proverbs and unusual visual concepts.

D1.justification: Section 1 replaces the Hugging Face access link with a project-website link for the dataset, code and synthetic data. Appendix A.2's generation prompts and $2.50 cost estimate, and Appendix C's hardware and training hyperparameters, were already present.

R1.justification: v4 adds Zhu et al.'s Self-supervised visual preference alignment to the references and the discussion contrasting existing-image approaches with Image-DPO's generated images. The broader research positioning and dataset comparisons remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 3 and 5 receive limited explanatory rewrites clarifying benchmark design, single-word evaluation and Score/Prior terminology. New appendix subsections are inserted, cross-references updated, and affiliation and acknowledgment text edited; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 10's original/realistic image pairs, Table 5's style results and Figure 14's failure cases. Existing displays are retained with updated captions, numbering and local placement; text and appendix layouts reflow without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The realistic-image experiment and expanded failure analysis provide useful additional benchmark validation and explanation, while clearer evaluation terminology improves readability. The small regenerated subset and absence of uncertainty estimates limit the new conclusions. The method, main results and theoretical argument remain unchanged.
